text:
marta: Heads up — after the GH Actions tweak to use `concurrency: group: ${{ github.head_ref }}` I saw Atlantis run a plan against `main` when PR #418 merged. Did the trigger semantics change? :thinking:
ashok: I noticed that too. The merge created a `workflow_run` that our other workflow picked up and it ran against the default branch. Seems the `on: pull_request` -> `workflow_run` handoff is the culprit.
sam: Can you paste the GH action trigger snippets? We might need an explicit `if` check for `github.event_name` or `github.head_ref`.
marta: here's the relevant part from `.github/workflows/infra-ci.yml` we changed yesterday:
```
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ["plan-and-apply"]
    types: [completed]
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.head_ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```
jing: The `workflow_run` event payload doesn't include `head_ref` the same way; when a PR is merged the workflow_run can reference the merge commit on `main`. So other workflows that rely on `head_ref` can end up running with `ref: main`.
kevin: For Atlantis we gate apply on `pull_request` events normally. But our alternate job that kicks off `atlantis plan` on `workflow_run` doesn't check `github.event.pull_request` existence. Quick fix: add `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || (github.event_name == 'workflow_run' && github.event.pull_requests && length(github.event.pull_requests) > 0)` to the job.
ashok: Or simpler, require `if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/')` on the plan job so it only runs for PR refs.
sam: Also double-check Atlantis repo config: we have `autoplan: when_modified: - '**/*.tf'` and `apply_requirements: [approved]`, but some repos have a custom `workflow` hook that triggers a remote plan. If that hook receives a `push` to `main` payload it will still create a plan.
marta: here's the Atlantis log snippet from the failed run:
```
2026-03-16T18:11:02Z INFO  atlantis: Received webhook: repo=infra, event=push, head_branch=main, pull_request=nil
2026-03-16T18:11:03Z INFO  atlantis: Creating plan task for repo infra at path ./clusters/us-west
```
jing: That makes sense — webhook was a `push` not a `pull_request`. The GH action `workflow_run` probably forwarded the merged commit.
kevin: Proposed GH action patch (cheap):
```
# job that triggers atlantis
if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/pull/')
```
ashok: For longer-term we should avoid `workflow_run` relay for infra workflows. Use the PR-level job matrix and call Atlantis directly from `pull_request` jobs. `workflow_run` is useful for cross-workflow coordination but it's fragile for branch semantics.
marta: OK can someone open a small PR to revert the `workflow_run` step and add the `if` guard? I can review quick.
sam: I'll open a PR in infra-ci with the `if` guard + comment explaining why. tagging @marta for review. :+1:
devops-bot: Started run: https://ci.redwood.internal/runs/82345 (rollback patch candidate).
marta: Thanks — once the PR is merged let's monitor Atlantis plans for the next few merges. If we see more false plans we can add an integration test in the infra repo that simulates merge events.
jing: FYI I'll add a short doc in the runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/ci-atlantis-workflow (notes about `workflow_run` pitfalls). :memo:
kevin: Also let's check secret propagation — some repos saw `K8S_SECRET_ENV` not present when the job switched to `workflow_run`. If we gate on `pull_request` those envs should be present as before.
marta: Great. Sam — ping here when PR is up.
sam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/infra-ci/pull/72 — small change, CI will run.
marta: Reviewed and lgtm, merging after checks pass. Thanks all. :tada:
